title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC — no Scripture for representation; forum tip before GAR 4
pass_a_gloss: Did Scripture reveal it? Show the verse. Can nature yield it? Give the reason. Beyond nature and Scripture I need not and should not agree to such an affirmation. Augustine's and Amyraut's wording will not yield it either. From 'every man by origin is nothing but Adam' it does not follow that God regarded all as one man in Adam, nor that Adam in sinning bore everyone's person. The learned man's claim that natural conjunction can fitly make someone suffer for another's crime fails in God's court unless there is also a sin-bond between them, or the punished party has a sin worthy of that penalty, or is himself a vessel of sins. The further claim that representation-unity makes Adam's sinning as if all had done the deed itself needs proof: not everything a representative does is imputed to the represented, consent or no. God covenanted with humankind in Noah and with Israel in Abraham; yet I do not think either man's merits or sins were charged to their offspring.
pass_b_english: Did God then reveal it in Scripture? Let the place be produced. Can it be gathered from nature? Let a reason be adduced. For to one affirming something of that kind I am neither bound nor is it expedient to assent beyond the book of nature and of Scripture. Nor indeed can it be gathered from the words of Augustine or of the most distinguished Amyraut. For what consequence is this: every man is by origin nothing but Adam—therefore all men were considered by God as one man in Adam—or, therefore Adam in sinning sustained the person of all men? What the learned man says, that a natural conjunction can be a fit cause why someone should undergo penalties for another's crime, is not true in the divine forum, unless there is also between them a conjunction of sin, or at least in the one who is punished a sin worthy of that penalty, or he himself is a vessel of sins. What he subjoins, that because of unity of representation Adam's sinning was the same as if all had committed the sin, needs proof. For not whatever one who represents another does is at once to be imputed to that other, whether he consents or does not consent. God struck a covenant with the human race in Noah, and with the Israelites in Abraham; yet of neither, I think, were good works or sins imputed to their posterity.
source_text: Idne igitur revelavit Deus in Scriptura? Proferatur locus. Potestne ex natura colligi? adferatur ratio. Affirmanti enim aliquid ejusmodi, praeter naturae & Scripturae librum assentiri nec teneor, nec expedit. Nec vero id ex Augustini aut Clariss. Amyraldi verbis colligi potest. Quae enim consequentia, omnis homo nihil est origine nisi Adam. Ergo omnes homines fuerunt a Deo considerati tanquam unus homo in Adam. Vel, Ergo Adamus in peccando sustinebat omnium hominum personam? Quod ait Vir Doctus, naturalem conjunctionem idoneam causam esse posse, cur aliquis pro alterius crimine poenis subjaceat, verum non est in foro divino; nisi aut sit etiam inter eos conjunctio peccati, aut saltem sit in eo, qui punitur, peccatum dignum illa poena, aut sit ipse peccatorum vas. Quod subjungit, propter unitatem repraesentationis, Adamo peccante idem fuisse, ac si omnes peccatum commisissent, probatione eget. Non enim quicquid facit qui alterum repraesentat, huic continuo sive consentiat, sive non consentiat, imputandum est. Pepigit Deus foedus cum genere humano in Noacho, & cum Israelitis in Abrahamo, neutrius tamen, opinor, aut bona opera aut peccata posteris imputata sunt.

choices.choice: Natural conjunction insufficient without sin-conjunction; Noah/Abraham analogy; stop before GAR 4
